content:
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo launched this week, and Apple has begun accepting iPhone Air and iPhone 17 as trade-ins for credit. However, the iPhone Air trade-in offer is a bit awkward, especially after this week's price increase.

Apple usually waits until new phones are released before accepting older models for trade-in. But the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 are exceptions — there is currently no iPhone Air 2 or iPhone 18, and new versions aren't expected until early next year at the earliest.

Nonetheless, Apple still wants to give iPhone Air and iPhone 17 users the opportunity to upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo. So both of these models, which are still sold by Apple but have no successors yet, are eligible for trade-in.

Take the iPhone 17 as an example: the phone got a $100 price hike this week, with the starting price adjusted to $899, while Apple offers up to $585 in trade-in credit.

The iPhone Air also got a $100 price hike this week, with the starting price rising to $1,099. So it's $200 more expensive than the iPhone 17 — what do you get in trade-in credit? Also $585. Truly shocking.

Apple's trade-in value chart is almost hard to believe — you'd suspect it's mislabeled. In reality, Apple is most likely basing it on market demand and component value. Thinking about it carefully, the fact that the iPhone Air uses nearly the same chip as the iPhone 17 Pro is really disappointing.

All in all, the iPhone Air costs $100 more for new buyers. But by Apple's standards, the iPhone Air's trade-in value is on par with a model that's $200 cheaper. That's seriously not great, Bob.
